rules.description: Questions must align with CBSE/NCERT syllabus for Classes 8–10. Reject if topic is irrelevant or outdated.
Match Bloom’s Taxonomy levels: Factual/Understanding (Easy/Medium), Application (Medium/Hard). Reject if too simplistic or lacks challenge.
Ensure questions are clearly worded and grammatically correct. Reject if ambiguous, verbose, or error-prone.
Include all required data and context. Reject if information is missing or relies on assumed knowledge.
Facts, formulas, terminology, and values must be scientifically accurate. Reject for factual or formulaic errors.
Avoid repeating previously asked questions. Reject for minimal variation or duplication.
Language must be neutral and inclusive. Reject if biased or culturally inappropriate.
Follow defined formats for SCQ, SA, LA, etc. Reject poorly structured or mismatched content.
Reject if concepts are incorrect, overly advanced (e.g. engineering physics), vague, or undefined.
Reject if too complex, lacks step-by-step logic, missing units, or relies on unrealistic assumptions.
Ensure all 4 options are consistent and logically related. Reject if answer is obvious or no correct option exists.
Reject if distractors are illogical or scientifically invalid.
Must be 20–30 words and justify 2 marks. Reject if too short, long, or confusing.
Reject if multiple correct forms exist without clarification.
Should be ~50–80 words and justify 3 marks. Reject if too short, too detailed, or improperly focused.
Reject if it has more than 3 unrelated sub-questions.
Should be 80–120 words and justify 5 marks. Reject if shallow, overly simple, or too broad.
Reject if it includes more than 5 sub-questions or lists unrelated points.
Passage must be 80–100 words and focused. Reject if too long, off-topic, or lacks clarity.
Reject if required visuals are missing, unlabeled, or unclear.
3 subjective sub-questions totaling 4 marks (e.g., 1+2+1). Reject if concepts are repeated or disconnected.
Reject if requiring external knowledge beyond NCERT textbook for the class.
